Hey guys!

I want to make sure my dog gets good food. I never go with a food with less than four stars on Dog Food Advisor, but I also have to get what's affordable for me.

I was in my local grocery store when I came across Freshpet Select in a little fridge in the pet section. I read the ingredients, checked it out on Dog Food Advisor and to my delight it had five stars.

I got three rolls and switched my girl to it. I had to switch her cold turkey (I know, that's terrible XC) as the food she was eating was giving her diarrhea.

Since switching her she had a few days of diarrhea but now her stools are looking better. Not great, but better.

I posted to a raw feeding group on facebook, asking if it would be a good idea to suppliment the food with bone to make sure her teeth stay in good shape.

I just got replies from a lot of people bashing the food. :/

So, I'm looking for second opinions!

I'm feeding my girl the rolled kind, specifically the beef recipe.

Any help is very appreciated!
What do you guys think about Freshpet Select?

Sorry for the super late reply; every time I go to check this subverse, I've been getting errors that Voat is down. Anyway, if it has 5 stars on Dog Food Advisor, I would trust the reviews and feel comfortable feeding it if your dog is doing well on it. It meets AAFCO standards, which is very important with any diet that you give your dog, since it ensures that your dog's nutrients are being met and he won't have any nutritional deficiencies that can lead to health problems down the road (and most raw feeders don't do that, unfortunately). My guess is that people were bashing the foods because they don't understand that carbs and fiber can actually be beneficial to dogs, especially those dogs with more sensitive stomachs who don't do well on an extremely high protein/fat diet like most raw food diets that you see on the Internet or Facebook groups. If your dog does well on it, I would definitely continue to feed it!

I also supplement my dog's food with bones to help with teeth cleaning. I give a bone like a chicken quarter or duck neck once or twice a week, not enough to throw off the balance of the food or affect his digestive system too much. Keep an eye on her poops, and if she gets too constipated or the poops are too hard or crumbly, back off on the bone.
